audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL state management (Prague transactional snapshots, account/storage operations, transient storage EIP-1153), EL EVM mechanics (STATICCALL EIP-214, CALL memory gas EIP-5, alt_bn128 precompiles EIP-1108, EIP-7702 set-code transactions), EL RPC (EIP-7910 eth_config, EIP-7927 history expiry), and CL topics (Altair light client sync, Deneb blob sidecar P2P, Bellatrix fork transition).

in_scope: State Transition (Prague state snapshots, account ops, storage ops, transient storage)
EVM Execution (STATICCALL, CALL memory gas, alt_bn128 precompiles)
Transaction Processing (EIP-7702 type-4 transactions, delegation indicators)
JSON-RPC Interface (EIP-7910 eth_config, EIP-7927 history expiry)
Gas Economics (EIP-1108 repricing, EIP-5 memory gas, EIP-7702 auth costs)
Blob Sidecar Gossip and Request/Response (Deneb P2P)
Beacon Block Validation (Deneb blob commitment limits)

threats: Submit malformed type-4 transactions with crafted authorization tuples
Query pre-merge history after expiry to trigger external data lookups
Submit transactions targeting precompiles with adversarial inputs
Send invalid blocks with manipulated state
Propagate blocks with excessive blob commitments
Re-entrancy attacks via CALL (mitigated by STATICCALL)
Storage collision attacks on delegated EOAs (EIP-7702)
Memory gas manipulation via dynamic return sizes (EIP-5)
Propose blocks with invalid blob sidecars
Equivocating blob sidecar publication across subnets

cl_vectors.entry_point: Beacon API / Light Client REST endpoints
threats: Serve false bootstrap data to light clients
Serve manipulated historical data from alternate sources

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component (calling contract within EVM execution context), not an external entity. Reclassified as internal EVM caller.
Internal EVM component (contract executing CALL opcode), not external to the system. Same as EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER.
Internal EVM component (sub-call target within EVM), not external to the system boundary.

Light client operator is the system administrator configuring the node. While external to the protocol, they are a trusted setup entity, not a runtime data source requiring trust modeling. Kept for completeness but treated as trusted setup.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC endpoint. Users can submit arbitrary transactions including type-4 (EIP-7702) with crafted authorization tuples, query node configuration (EIP-7910), and request historical data (EIP-7927). All input is potentially malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker exploiting exposed RPC for reconnaissance (EIP-7910 config leak), DDoS via repeated requests, or replaying EIP-7702 authorization tuples. No authentication required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers can send arbitrary blob sidecars, beacon blocks, and light client updates. All data requires cryptographic validation (KZG proofs, proposer signatures, sync committee signatures).

trusted_external_entities.name: Requesting Peer via P2P Request/Response
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated peers requesting blob data. Must enforce rate limits and retention window checks (MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS). Potential for resource exhaustion.

trusted_external_entities.name: Full Node via Beacon API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Full nodes serving light client data are untrusted. Bootstrap data, updates, and finality updates must be verified against trusted block roots and sync committee signatures. A compromised node could serve stale or false data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Compromised Node via eth_config RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: A malicious or compromised node queried for configuration comparison (EIP-7910) can return false configuration data, misleading validators about fork readiness.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted External Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External contracts invoked via CALL may contain malicious code attempting re-entrancy, state modification in static context, or adversarial precompile inputs. STATICCALL (EIP-214) provides sandboxing. EIP-7702 delegation introduces new attack surface where delegated code executes in EOA context.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC (Type-4)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Submitter of EIP-7702 type-4 transactions. Authorization tuples must be validated: chain ID, nonce bounds, signature recovery, s-value malleability, authority code state. Invalid authorizations are skipped (not reverted), but format validation is strict.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attacker Replaying EIP-7702 Authorizations
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (replayed authorization tuples in type-4 transactions)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker attempting to replay previously signed authorization tuples. Nonce-based replay protection ensures nonce mismatch causes skip. Cross-chain replay possible if chain_id=0 was used.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Historical Data Source
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: e2store archive / Portal Network / EIP-7801 DevP2P protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: After EIP-7927 history expiry, pre-merge data is retrieved from external sources. Data must be validated against known block hashes. Untrusted sources could serve manipulated historical data.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full request validation required: rate limiting for eth_config (recommended 1s interval), transaction format validation, authorization tuple validation for type-4 transactions. Access should be restricted to trusted interfaces where possible.
Rate limiting must be enforced to prevent DDoS. Endpoint access should be restricted to trusted interfaces only. Configuration data exposure is an information leak risk.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P gossip blob_sidecar_{subnet_id} and beacon_block topics
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full cryptographic validation required: blob index < MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK, correct subnet mapping, valid proposer signature, valid Merkle inclusion proof, valid KZG proof, blob_kzg_commitments count <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK.
Enforce MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS (768) limit. Verify requested slots are within MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS retention window. Return ResourceUnavailable error for out-of-window requests.

Bootstrap must be verified against trusted block root (out-of-band). Updates require valid sync committee aggregate signatures (>= 2/3 threshold). Finality updates must contain valid finality proof. Light client must verify all data cryptographically before accepting.
Configuration data from any single node must be cross-checked against multiple sources and the official specification. Never trust a single node's configuration response for fork readiness decisions.

STATICCALL (EIP-214) enforces read-only execution: CREATE, LOG, SSTORE, SELFDESTRUCT, CALL-with-value are prohibited. STATIC flag must propagate correctly through nested calls. For EIP-7702 delegated EOAs, delegation resolves only one level. Precompile inputs (EIP-1108) must be validated: point-on-curve check, input length validation.

Type-4 transaction validation: non-empty authorization list, non-null destination, sender must be EOA or delegated. Each authorization: chain_id must be 0 or current, nonce < 2^64-1, valid ecrecover with MAGIC prefix, s <= secp256k1n/2, authority code empty or existing delegation, authority nonce matches.

Nonce-based replay protection: authority nonce is incremented after each successful authorization, so replayed tuples will fail nonce match. Cross-chain replay is possible if chain_id=0 was used in the original authorization.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: e2store / Portal Network / EIP-7801 data retrieval
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All externally sourced historical data must be validated against known canonical block hashes, transaction roots, and receipt roots. Data integrity verification is mandatory before serving to RPC clients.
